newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast late prods flatten amid thin trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast late prods flatten amid thin trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast product prices flattened late Thursday amid thin talk and a lack of concern about supply following an early week fire at Texaco's Los Angeles refinery.
West Coast players shrugged off a second-straight day of higher heating oil futures, which ended up 2.20 cents at 73.40 cents a gallon.
More importantly, NYMEX crude, which drives the isolated western markets more than prods, rallied 29 cents to $24.41 a barrel, leaving traders concerned about squeezed margins.
"Crude levels are strong, the (NYMEX) was up, but nothing really happened," a trader said, explaining thin buying.

Unleaded conventional gasoline in Los Angeles was flat at 59/60 cents a gallon, while CARB-grade stayed 62.50/63.50 cents a gallon. Flush gasoline supplies, which the API showed 533,000 barrels higher last week, helped neutralize the effect of higher futures.
The market got an early week bounce after a fire damaged a Texaco hydrotreater in Los Angeles. Wholesale prices rose as much as two cents on Monday.
